almond: Almond: sweet marzipan and bitter almond — cherry-like, powdery and distinctly gourmand.
amber: Amber: warm, resinous and slightly sweet — a golden glow from labdanum, benzoin and vanilla, never the stone itself.
ambery: Ambery: a softer take on amber — warm vanilla-resin glow with a honeyed, slightly powdery sweetness.
animalic: Animalic: raw, primal warmth — civet, castoreum and leather notes that smell of skin, musk and wild fur.
aquatic: Aquatic: cool water and sea breeze — clean, ozonic freshness that smells of waves and wet stones.
aromatic: Aromatic: crisp, green herbs — lavender, rosemary, sage and thyme — like a Mediterranean garden after rain.
balsamic: Balsamic: soft, warm resins — Peru balsam, tolu and benzoin with a sweet, slightly powdery glow.
bright: Bright: luminous and sparkling — citrus, aldehydes and light florals that feel like sunlight on skin.
caramel: Caramel: burnt sugar and butterscotch — golden, sticky sweetness that warms any gourmand blend.
chocolate: Chocolate: dark cocoa — bitter-sweet, velvety and indulgent, never quite as sweet as the real thing.
citrus: Citrus: bright, sparkling freshness from bergamot, lemon, orange and grapefruit — the zesty lift of the opening minutes.
coffee: Coffee: dark roasted beans — bitter, rich and energising, from espresso shot to sweet coffee liqueur.
creamy: Creamy: soft, smooth and milky — coconut, sandalwood and white florals blended into a velvety texture.
dark: Dark: shadowy and brooding — deep woods, smoke, leather and resins with no bright edges.
dry: Dry: crisp and unsweet — woods, vetiver and tea notes with all moisture and sugar stripped away.
earthy: Earthy: damp soil, roots and moss — vetiver and patchouli at their most natural, like a forest floor after rain.
elegant: Elegant: refined and polished — soft florals, fine woods and powdery musk in perfect, understated balance.
floral: Floral: the classic scent of fresh-cut flowers — jasmine, rose, lily and geranium blended into a blooming bouquet.
fresh: Fresh: clean and airy — green leaves, light citrus and water notes that smell of a breeze through an open window.
fresh-spicy: Fresh spicy: pepper, ginger and cardamom over a crisp green base — cool and energising rather than cosy.
fruity: Fruity: juicy, mouthwatering brightness — pineapple, pear, berries and citrus, like a fruit market in full colour.
gourmand: Gourmand: deliciously edible — chocolate, caramel, coffee and vanilla blended into dessert you can wear.
green: Green: cut grass, crushed leaves and galbanum — the sharp, dewy smell of a garden at dawn.
herbal: Herbal: green kitchen-garden freshness — basil, thyme and sage, leafy and naturally bracing.
honey: Honey: golden, syrupy sweetness — rich beeswax warmth with a faintly animalic, sunlit glow.
iris: Iris: elegant, powdery orris root — cool, cosmetic and violet-like, like expensive face powder.
juicy: Juicy: ripe, mouthwatering fruit — the burst of biting into a peach or pineapple, fresh and vivid.
lactonic: Lactonic: milky, coconut-like creaminess — the soft white flesh of coconut or warm milk on skin.
lavender: Lavender: clean, aromatic purple flowers — fresh, slightly camphorous and calming, the backbone of the fougère family.
leather: Leather: smooth, warm and animalic — like a new leather jacket or a saddler's workshop, often paired with smoke or tobacco.
leathery: Leathery: a suede-soft variation on leather — warm, smooth and slightly smoky, like well-worn gloves.
marine: Marine: salt spray and ocean air — briny, mineral freshness that smells of the open sea.
metallic: Metallic: cold, sharp and mineral — a steely, aldehydic edge that smells of wet coins and clean glass.
mossy: Mossy: damp oakmoss and forest floor — green, earthy and slightly bitter, the soul of the classic chypre.
musky: Musky: soft, skin-like warmth — the clean comfort of freshly laundered clothes with a subtle animal purr underneath.
mysterious: Mysterious: shadowy and elusive — incense, dark woods and spice that shift as you try to pin them down.
nutty: Nutty: toasted almonds, hazelnuts and pistachio — warm, buttery richness without full sweetness.
opulent: Opulent: the grandest version of rich — layered amber, oud and florals, unapologetically lavish.
oriental: Oriental: opulent warmth — amber, vanilla, spices and resins layered into something rich, dark and dramatic.
oud: Oud: deep, resinous agarwood — smoky, leathery and faintly animalic, the dark heart of Middle Eastern perfumery.
ozonic: Ozonic: the smell of air itself — clean, electric freshness like rain on hot pavement or laundry on a line.
patchouli: Patchouli: rich, dark and earthy — dried leaves with a sweet, musty depth that anchors oriental and chypre perfumes.
powdery: Powdery: soft, dry and velvety — iris, violet and rice powder, like face powder on vintage lace.
resinous: Resinous: thick, warm tree resins — frankincense, myrrh and opoponax, sticky and glowing like candlelit amber.
rich: Rich: full-bodied and opulent — heavy resins, dark florals and woods that feel expensive and dense.
rose: Rose: lush and romantic — from delicate tea rose to dark, jammy Turkish rose, always unmistakably floral.
smokey: Smokey: a mellow, drifting haze of incense and woodsmoke — softer and hazier than a sharp smoky note.
smoky: Smoky: dry woods, incense and birch tar — the smell of a distant bonfire clinging to a leather jacket.
soapy: Soapy: freshly washed skin and bar soap — clean aldehydes and white musk that smell simply of being clean.
spicy: Spicy: a kick of black pepper, saffron and clove — piquant, lively and full of contrast.
sweet: Sweet: a sugary, candy-like impression from vanilla, tonka, honey and ripe fruit — warm and inviting without being edible.
tobacco: Tobacco: honeyed, leathery dried tobacco leaf — sweet pipe smoke with a warm, golden glow.
tropical: Tropical: sun-warmed exotic fruit — coconut, mango and tiare flower, like a beach holiday in a bottle.
vanilla: Vanilla: creamy, sweet and comforting — soft vanilla pods with a faintly boozy warmth underneath.
warm-spicy: Warm spicy: cinnamon, clove, cardamom and nutmeg — the cosy heat of mulled wine and baking spices.
waxy: Waxy: beeswax and candlelight — warm, honeyed and slightly powdery, like the inside of a chapel.
white-floral: White floral: heady, creamy blooms — jasmine, tuberose, orange blossom and gardenia with a narcotic sweetness.
woody: Woody: the warm, dry backbone of sandalwood, cedar, vetiver and pine — like the inside of a cedar closet or freshly shaved timber.
